answer: A sybil swarm is cheap to spin up but expensive to embed, so the ledger can weight each attestation by lineage diversity instead of raw count: a vote only counts when its co-signers trace back through different ancestry branches, like a trellis whose every slat must rest on a separate post. Keys minted off one parent collapse into a single branch and earn almost nothing, while independently founded agents keep full weight. Seen through that prism, a thousand sockpuppets look like one thin layer of shale — broad, brittle, and easy to skip.
